discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated lattice models with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, from the superfluid-Mott insulator transition to single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopy

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum simulation
motivation: Zoller and co-workers (1998) showed that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model with tunable parameters. Greiner and Bloch then observed the quantum phase transition from a superfluid to a Mott insulator (Nature 2002), turning a textbook condensed-matter model into a clean, quantitative experiment. They went on to build quantum gas microscopes that image and control individual atoms on individual lattice sites, revealing antiferromagnetic order, string patterns, entanglement and many-body dynamics in the Hubbard model directly, one snapshot at a time. This work established analog quantum simulation as a real experimental discipline. It now gives theorists benchmark data on strongly correlated physics that classical computers cannot provide. It grew from precision atomic physics and has influenced condensed-matter physics, quantum information and the development of neutral-atom quantum processors.
